narrative:
The model determined that you have a 34% chance of representing a bad credit risk. Because this probability exceeded the bank's acceptance threshold, your loan application was denied.

The three factors that most strongly influenced this outcome were the status of your checking account, the installment rate as a percentage of your disposable income, and the purpose of the loan. Your checking account status had the largest impact and pushed the decision toward denial. Having a negative balance (under 0 DM) is relatively uncommon among approved applicants—only 12.6% of them show this status—whereas most approved borrowers have either no checking account or a positive balance. This signaled higher risk to the model.

Your requested loan purpose (used car) worked in your favor, pulling the prediction toward approval. Among approved loans, used-car financing is less common than loans for radio/TV or furniture, and the model viewed this purpose as lower risk.

The installment rate also helped your case by modestly reducing the predicted risk. At 2% of your disposable income, your rate sits below the 3% average seen among approved applicants, indicating a more manageable repayment burden.

While these factors were weighed together, the negative signal from your checking account outweighed the positive contributions, leading to denial. To improve future applications, focus on clearing your checking account to a positive balance before reapplying, as this appears to be the dominant driver of the outcome. Consider starting with a smaller loan amount or providing additional proof of repayment capacity.
